body:
Fixes #2164

## Summary

By default a Docker-isolated task is handed the operator's real subscription: `~/.claude`, `~/.claude.json`, `~/.codex`, `~/.agents` and `~/.config/gh` are bind-mounted into the container. The agent inside holds the raw vendor OAuth credential, can spend the subscription without limit, and leaves no record of what it did beyond what it chose to write itself.

`--use-router` (**experimental**) withholds those mounts. The credentials stay in a single reference-counted `hive-mind-router` sidecar on an internal Docker network, each task is joined to that network and given its own `la_sk_…` token scoped to the one repository it works on, and every model request lands in that token's own redacted log.

```bash
solve https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/42 --isolation docker --use-router
```

Nothing changes without the flag — that is deliberate (R9): this is opt-in isolation, not a migration.

Every requirement was analysed against first-party evidence before any code was written; the analysis, the pinned upstream sources and the checksummed evidence set are in [`docs/case-studies/issue-2164/`](docs/case-studies/issue-2164/README.md).

## Upstream first (R16), and what it unblocked

The audit of router `v0.105.0` found four gaps, and per the issue they were reported upstream before any workaround was written here: [router#260](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/260) (stored OpenAI-compatible providers ignored by automatic routing), [#261](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/261) (git transport bypasses the policy engine), [#262](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/262) (per-deployment GitHub credential and policy), [#263](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/263) (no TLS listener, so `gh` cannot use the router as a host).

**All four were fixed upstream on 2026-08-21** and shipped in `v0.106.0`–`v0.109.0`. This PR pins `ghcr.io/link-assistant/router:0.119.0`, which is what makes R11, R12 and the transport half of R13 deliverable here rather than deferred. Re-measuring produced three further upstream reports — [#270](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/270), [#271](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/271), [#272](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/272) — **all three since fixed**. A re-audit against `v0.119.0` on 2026-08-26 filed four more: [#322](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/322), [#323](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/323), [#324](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/324) (fixed; #323 partially — tier aliases declined by design) and [#329](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/329), which is the one remaining limit (see [Limits](#what-is-not-covered)).

## What changed

| #           | Requirement                              | Delivered by                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| R1, R9, R10 | The flag, opt-in, marked experimental    | `--use-router` in `SOLVE_OPTION_DEFINITIONS` with the `[EXPERIMENTAL]` prefix; `HIVE_MIND_USE_ROUTER=1` carries the decision into the bot and nested runs                                                                           |
| R2, R3      | Router is the only point of contact      | `src/router-isolation.lib.mjs` suppresses the credential mounts at the seam in `src/isolation-runner.lib.mjs`; the sidecar alone mounts the subscription                                                                            |
| R4          | Verify the router actually supports this | Part 2 of the case study, quoted against the pinned router README, then re-measured against `v0.109.0` in `docs/case-studies/issue-2164/data/measurements/`                                                                        |
| R5          | Run only while a task needs it           | Lease-counted sidecar in `src/router-sidecar.lib.mjs`; the bot's maintenance tick reconciles leases against Docker and stops idle routers                                                                                           |
| R6          | One token per task, one log per task     | One `router tokens issue` per session id, scoped with `--github-repo`, revoked on release, never shared                                                                                                                             |
| R7          | Merge session data back at end of task   | `src/router-session-drain.lib.mjs` — `docker cp` works on stopped containers, so a crashed task is drained as well as a clean one                                                                                                   |
| R8, R14     | Keep the logs, make them readable        | Named volume `hive-mind-router-data` that **no code path removes**; `src/router-logs.lib.mjs` reads it with or without a running router                                                                                             |
| R11         | `--model formal-ai` through the router   | `registerFormalAiWithRouter()` stores the Formal AI sidecar as an OpenAI-compatible provider (`router providers add`); the router dispatches on the model id, so other tasks are unaffected                                         |
| R12         | Route `gh` and `git`                     | The sidecar terminates TLS with a certificate naming `api.github.com`, the task resolves that host to the router, and each client is handed the CA the way it expects (`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, `http.<url>.sslCAInfo`). An unmodified `gh` is mediated and the task holds no GitHub credential |
| R13         | Block destructive git operations         | Three layers: branch protection; a read-only `pre-push` hook (`src/git-push-guard.lib.mjs`); and the router's `/git/*` transport, which refuses ref deletions with HTTP 403 (measured in `data/measurements/git-transport.log`) and, from router `0.110.0`, non-fast-forward updates as well. The gh-API half is partial — see Limits |
| R15         | Document log collection system-wide      | [`docs/COLLECTING-LOGS.md`](docs/COLLECTING-LOGS.md) ×4 languages and `examples/collect-logs.mjs`, both driven by one `describeSystemLogLocations()`                                                                                |
| R16         | Report upstream gaps first               | router#260–#263 filed before the corresponding code; #270–#272 filed after re-measuring `v0.109.0` (all fixed); #322, #323, #324, #329 filed in the 2026-08-26 re-audit of `v0.119.0`                                                                                                                                  |
| R17         | Case study                               | [`docs/case-studies/issue-2164/`](docs/case-studies/issue-2164/README.md) with a checksummed `MANIFEST.md` and the raw probe logs                                                                                                   |

Along the way, `src/docker-sidecar.lib.mjs` extracts the container lifecycle both sidecars share, and `src/formal-ai-sidecar.lib.mjs` is rewritten on top of it — same behaviour, one implementation.

The signing secret never enters a task's environment, is never logged, and `examples/collect-logs.mjs` deliberately refuses to copy the state directory into an evidence archive.

## What is *not* covered

These limits are documented in [`docs/ROUTER.md`](docs/ROUTER.md) **and printed before every routed run**, so nobody discovers them by being breached:

- **Destructive GitHub API calls are blocked by method, not by effect** — [router#329](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/329). Every `DELETE`, forced REST ref update and destructive GraphQL mutation is refused. The same outcomes spelled differently are not: `PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/branches/{b}/protection` replaces a protection object wholesale, `PUT .../rulesets/{id}` relaxes a ruleset, `POST .../transfer` moves the repository, and `PATCH /repos/{o}/{r}` can flip `visibility`, `archived` or `default_branch`. Branch protection is reachable this way, so it is a strong default rather than a control a routed task cannot touch. Bounded in practice by the permissions of the `gh` credential the router presents upstream.
- **A force push _is_ now blocked**, contrary to what earlier revisions of this PR said. [router#272](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/272) was fixed in [router#273](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/pull/273) and shipped in `v0.110.0`, seventeen minutes after the comment here describing it as open. The router asks GitHub's compare API whether the proposed tip is ahead of the current one and fails closed when it cannot tell.
- **The Formal AI sidecar's own upstream calls are not routed.** `--model formal-ai` reaches Formal AI through the router, but if that server itself calls a vendor API, that leg leaves the sidecar directly.
- **Non-Claude tools are less exercised.** codex, gemini and qwen are wired through the router's OpenAI-compatible surface; only Claude Code has an end-to-end probe in `experiments/issue-2164/`.
- **Model aliases are rejected** — the router ships no alias table by design ([router#192](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/192)) and declined to add tier resolution ([router#323](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/323)), so `--model claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` works where `--model sonnet` does not. Since `0.115.0` the refusal lists the ids that would have worked. This affects the tier-shaped surface generally — `--plan`, `--escalate` and the fallback chains all name tiers — so pin dated ids on a routed run. The remedy is on our side (export `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL` resolved from `GET /v1/models`) and is deliberately left out of this PR pending a measurement; see the case study's re-audit section.
- **`HIVE_MIND_ROUTER_GITHUB=0`, or an external router**, leaves the task with its own `gh` credential; an external router has no container network of ours to intercept in and needs `HIVE_MIND_ROUTER_GH_HOST`.

## Tests

Five regression suites, all in the default suite and all passing locally, alongside `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:duplication`:

| Suite                                        | What it pins down                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tests/test-issue-2164-router-isolation.mjs` | Credentials are actually suppressed when routed and untouched when not; GitHub interception, CA trust and the git routing config are wired as documented; every coverage gap is warned about      |
| `tests/test-issue-2164-router-sidecar.mjs`   | Lease counting, idle stop, launch grace, one repo-scoped token per task, the Formal AI provider registration (R11), and that the signing secret never reaches a task                                                                                      |
| `tests/test-issue-2164-session-drain.mjs`    | Session data is archived before the token is revoked, including from stopped containers                                                                                                                       |
| `tests/test-issue-2164-log-collection.mjs`   | The logs are still readable after the sidecar is gone, collection cannot damage what it collects, and the docs list matches the code's list                                                                    |
| `tests/test-issue-2164-git-push-guard.mjs`   | Runs the hook against a **real repository and a real remote**: force-push after `git reset --hard` and `push --delete` both fail, the remote still holds the discarded commit, an ordinary push still succeeds |

Behaviour that only a live router can show — TLS interception, the git transport's 403, the Formal AI provider — is recorded as raw probe output in [`docs/case-studies/issue-2164/data/measurements/`](docs/case-studies/issue-2164/data/measurements/), with the probe scripts kept in `experiments/issue-2164/`.

## Docs

- [`docs/ROUTER.md`](docs/ROUTER.md) (+ `ru`/`zh`/`hi`) — what changes, how it works, the audit trail, configuration, destructive git operations, coverage gaps
- [`docs/COLLECTING-LOGS.md`](docs/COLLECTING-LOGS.md) (+ `ru`/`zh`/`hi`) — every log location in the system, not just the router's (R15)
- [`docs/case-studies/issue-2164/README.md`](docs/case-studies/issue-2164/README.md) — requirement-by-requirement analysis, online research, prior art, the upstream gap reports and the post-upgrade measurements

A `minor` changeset is included.
title: feat(router): route AI subscriptions, gh and git through hive-mind-router with per-task tokens (EXPERIMENTAL)
